ruled_out_vectors.vector: KV-1: Zero-price bypass in validateHandlerOrder via computeRatioX96 overflow
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: computeRatioX96 CAN return 0 for extreme price ratios (confirmed: calculateFixedInput(1, type(uint160).max) produces output that overflows computeRatioX96). However, validateHandlerOrder only validates ORDER CREATION (not fills). The fill path goes through beforeSwap/afterSwap which has explicit zero-check (AMMStandardHook.sol:847). Even if an extreme-price order passes creation validation, filling it requires a willing taker providing enormous output. No extraction path exists.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: KV-2: Direct handler call bypasses beforeSwap/afterSwap pricing enforcement
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: ammHandleTransfer checks msg.sender == AMM at line 230. Direct calls revert with CLOBTransferHandler__CallbackMustBeFromAMM. openOrder is externally callable but only creates orders — it does not execute fills. Order creation goes through _enforceTokenHooks which calls validateHandlerOrder. The fill path always goes through the AMM which triggers beforeSwap/afterSwap hooks.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: KV-3: Settings sync gap in CLOBTransferHandler.setTokenSettings
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: CLOBTransferHandler does not have a setTokenSettings function. Token settings are fetched from the AMM via ILimitBreakAMM(AMM).getTokenSettings() in _enforceTokenHooks (line 582-583). The handler reads settings on each call rather than caching them, so there is no stale memSettings issue. CreatorHookSettingsRegistry is in AMMStandardHook, not in CLOBTransferHandler.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: KV-4: Transient storage leak in DIRECT_SWAP_BEFORE_SWAP_AMOUNT_SLOT
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: The slot is written in beforeSwap (line 839) and read in afterSwap (line 843-844). The AMM calls beforeSwap then afterSwap sequentially for each swap — they do not interleave. Transient storage is automatically cleared at end of transaction (EIP-1153/tstorish). The slot (0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF) is a single global slot but sequential processing prevents cross-swap contamination. This is also FP pattern #1 from audit memory: 'Transient storage slot overwrite — by-design'.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: FixedHelper.sol line 69 operator precedence bug (redeposited0 | redeposited1 == 0)
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Solidity's bitwise OR (|) has higher precedence than equality (==), so the expression correctly parses as (redeposited0 | redeposited1) == 0 — matching the intended behavior. Verified with Forge test across all 4 combinations (both zero, both nonzero, one zero each). No exploitation path.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: CLOBHelper.calculateFixedInput rounding direction leaks value to makers
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: calculateFixedInput uses mulDivRoundingUp (rounds UP output to maker) vs SingleProviderHelper which uses mulDiv (rounds DOWN). Confirmed: at adversarial price (2.25), 1-wei fills produce 3 wei output vs exact 2.25. However, gas cost per fill (~600 trillion wei at 30 gwei) is 300 trillion times the rounding leak (~2 wei per fill). Even with 1M fills, total leak is 750K wei (< $0.01). Not economically exploitable — falls under dust-level precision threshold.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: FeeHelper unchecked subtraction in output fee calculation
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: FeeHelper._calculateBPSFeeWithRecipientAndProtocolFeeSwapByOutput (line 220-224) has unchecked feeAmount -= protocolFeeAmount. protocolFeeAmount = mulDivRoundingUp(feeAmount, protocolFeeBPS, MAX_BPS). Since protocolFeeBPS <= MAX_BPS (enforced by setExchangeProtocolFeeOverride at ModuleAdmin.sol:91), protocolFeeAmount <= feeAmount always holds. No underflow possible.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: 100% fee asymmetry between input and output swaps
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Input allows exchangeFeeBPS == MAX_BPS (100%), output rejects it (>= MAX_BPS). This is intentional design: 100% input fee means all input goes to fee (0 reaches swap), which is safe. 100% output fee would require division by zero in mulDivRoundingUp(amountIn, 10000, 0). Known gotcha, documented in codebase.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: FullMath.mulDiv phantom overflow creating free tokens
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Tested mulDiv(max, max, max) = max, mulDiv with intermediate overflow (a=max/2+1, b=3, d=3 = a). mulDivRoundingUp always >= mulDiv (verified by Halmos symbolic execution: check_roundingUpAlwaysGtOrEq PASSED, 18 paths explored). No phantom overflow found.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: SqrtPriceMath price direction incorrect for getNextSqrtPriceFromInput/Output
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Verified all 4 variants: (1) adding token0 zeroForOne=true decreases price, (2) adding token1 zeroForOne=false increases price, (3) zero amount preserves price, (4) outputting token0 !zeroForOne increases price. All directionally correct.

Verified: getAmount0Delta(roundUp=true) >= getAmount0Delta(roundUp=false), same for getAmount1Delta. Equal prices return 0 for both. Rounding favors protocol (user pays more when roundUp=true for input, receives less when roundUp=false for output).

Verified round-trip at 5 representative ticks (-100000, -1000, 0, 1000, 100000) and every 1000th tick from -800000 to 800000 (1601 ticks total). All pass: getSqrtPriceAtTick(tick) -> getTickAtSqrtPrice returns original tick. Note: MIN_TICK/MAX_TICK boundary has different behavior (getSqrtPriceAtTick returns MIN/MAX_SQRT_RATIO which is AT the boundary, causing getTickAtSqrtPrice to revert) — this is expected Uniswap V3 behavior.
